label: r2c1
name: Flip, 2 PPO epochs
hypothesis: Same network and recipe as the best trial, but with ppo_epochs set to 2. This buys about 1.85x more environment steps (about 118 updates). Training success was still rising at the end, so the agent looks sample-limited, and fresh data should help it generalise to new designs more than extra passes over old data. Refuted if dev success is not above 0.864 by more than about 3 points, or if the training curve flattens earlier.
last_analysis: The flip of the column axis is what made learning possible: 0 without it, 0.64–0.94 with it, and learned column mixing without it reached only 0.04. Among recipes, 2 PPO epochs is best so far (r2c1, 0.941, seeds 0.949 and 0.934). 4 epochs gave 0.864, and 1 epoch lost a seed (0.934 and 0.000), so too many updates risk instability. A longer horizon (gamma 0.99) scored 0.902 with 2 epochs. Extra trunk depth plus global broadcast (0.711) and the per-cell verify head (0.856) both did worse; their extra compute cost samples. Going from 64 to 128 updates helped in round 1. Remaining dev failures are rare order or overhang errors (about 0.14 cells outside the target per episode). This is the last round, so two candidates are single-change recipe refinements of r2c1 and one is a cheap new architecture idea with unchanged compute.
